case_bezel.name: Case and Bezel
case_bezel.description: The metal body of the watch and the ring around the crystal. The case holds and protects the movement.
facts: Cases are commonly made of stainless steel, titanium or precious metals.
The bezel is the ring that holds the crystal in place.

crystal.name: Crystal
crystal.description: The clear cover over the dial.
facts: Watch crystals are usually sapphire, mineral glass or acrylic.
Sapphire crystal is very scratch resistant.

dial.name: Dial
dial.description: The face of the watch with hour markers and the chronograph subdials.
facts: A chronograph dial usually has small subdials that count elapsed seconds, minutes or hours.
Markers around the edge show the hours and minutes.

hands.name: Hands
hands.description: The hour, minute and seconds hands, plus the smaller hand used for the chronograph.
facts: The hour hand is shorter than the minute hand.
On a chronograph, a central seconds hand often runs only when the stopwatch is started.

pushers.name: Pushers and Crown
pushers.description: The buttons on the side of the case. The pushers start, stop and reset the chronograph; the crown sets the time.
facts: A typical chronograph has two pushers: one to start/stop and one to reset.
The crown is turned to set the time and, on mechanical watches, to wind the mainspring.

case_back.name: Case Back
case_back.description: The back cover of the case that seals the movement inside.
facts: Case backs are screwed, snapped or bolted on.
Some have a transparent window to show the movement.

strap.name: Strap
strap.description: The band that holds the watch on the wrist.
facts: This strap combines a carbon-fibre-look outer layer with a plastic band.
Straps attach to the case at the lugs, usually with spring bars.

buckle.name: Buckle (Clasp)
buckle.description: The fastener that closes the strap around the wrist.
facts: Common types are the pin (tang) buckle and the folding (deployant) clasp.
